title: Which is the largest number dividing 306 and 36?
description: Six choices are given, and the largest number that divides both three hundred six and thirty six is needed. The highest common factor is found from the prime counts and checked by division.
teaching_notes: One idea: the largest number that divides two numbers is their highest common factor, found by taking the smaller count of each prime. Ask the class to name one number that divides both before the working is shown. Watch for students who choose the biggest choice, or who choose a number that divides only one of the two.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q7
video_script.why: The child has found the highest common factor to cut equal pieces and now finds it from the prime counts of two larger numbers and picks it from a list of choices.
video_script.substitution: Break 306 and 36 into primes, take the smaller count of each prime, and pick the product from the choices.
video_script.anchor: The numbers 306 and 36 written side by side, with six choices listed below them.
video_script.payoff_line: The largest number that divides both is eighteen
never_show: 36 as the number that divides both
maths_rules: smaller counts: 2 once, 3 twice, 17 zero times
check: 306 ÷ 18 = 17 and 36 ÷ 18 = 2; 17 and 2 share no factor except 1, so no larger number divides both
larger choices 36, 612, 360 do not divide both; 3 and 2 are smaller
video_script.design: One idea: the largest number that divides both numbers is their highest common factor. The two numbers stay on the board and the smaller prime counts are lit.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We are given two numbers, three hundred six and thirty six.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The choices are thirty six, six hundred twelve, eighteen, three, two and three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which choice is the largest number that divides both of them?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Some numbers divide both of two numbers, and one of them is the largest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The largest number that divides both is called their highest common factor.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We find it by breaking each number into primes, and taking the smaller count of each prime.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

beats.on_screen: To find: the largest number that divides both

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the largest number that divides both. We solve it the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: we need the HCF of 306 and 36

marks.m1: the words HCF of 306 and 36 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, we need the highest common factor of three hundred six and thirty six.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, three hundred six is two times three times three times seventeen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty six is two times two times three times three.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: smaller counts: 2 once, 3 twice, 17 zero times; HCF = 2 × 3 × 3 = 18

marks.m1: 2 is lit once, since 306 has one 2 and 36 has two
marks.m2: 3 is lit twice, and 17 is lit zero times

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, take the smaller count of each prime. Two appears once in the first number and twice in the second, so we take it once.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three appears twice in both, so we take it twice. Seventeen is only in the first number, so we take it zero times.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The highest common factor is two times three times three, which is eighteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: 306 ÷ 18 = 17 and 36 ÷ 18 = 2; 17 and 2 share no factor except 1; the larger choices 36, 612 and 360 do not divide both

marks.m2: 17 and 2 are set side by side with no shared factor except 1
marks.m3: 36, 612 and 360 are crossed out in the choices

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check. Three hundred six divided by eighteen is seventeen. Thirty six divided by eighteen is two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seventeen and two share no factor except one, so no larger number divides both.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The larger choices do not divide both numbers.

marks.m1: the answer (c) 18 is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The largest number that divides both is eighteen.
